claim: GR00T N1.7 fine-tunes on one 24 GB RTX 3090 Ti: NVIDIA's own settings fit only with the DiT action head frozen, at batch 8 (none with it trained), and with three memory savers NVIDIA's launcher does not expose (the frozen backbone in bf16, the DiT's activations recomputed, AdamW state in 8 bits) the full default fine-tune, 1.62B trainable parameters, fits at batch 58, 24.4 samples/s.
argv: START=8 gr00t-smoke.sh maxbatch full-lean (batches 8 to 32; aborted at 64 by a script fault, see caveats)
instrument: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 3090 Ti, 24,564 MiB, driver 610.88, PCIe 4.0 x8, WSL2 (Linux 6.18.54.1-microsoft-standard-WSL2), 31 GB of RAM in the VM; Isaac-GR00T c56f541 in its own uv env (Python 3.12, torch 2.9.0+cu128, transformers 4.57.3, flash-attn 2.8.3, bitsandbytes 0.50.2, DeepSpeed removed); BF16 with TF32

inputs.dataset: Isaac-GR00T demo_data/cube_to_bowl_5 (SO-101, front and wrist cameras, AV1, 5 episodes, 4,148 frames)

nvidia_settings_dit_trained.result: does not fit at any batch: batch 32 and batch 8 both filled the card before the first step completed (fp32 weights 12.6 GB, gradients 6.5 GB and AdamW state 13 GB come to about 32 GB before activations)

frozen.settings: NVIDIA's (fp32 weights, AdamW), the DiT frozen (--no-tune-diffusion-model)

Studio open; at the cutoff exactly

outcome.desktop_baseline_mib: 1,105 to 1,319 with the Studio closed; 1,889 with it open
outcome.nvidia_reference: Isaac-GR00T README, N1.7 single-GPU table (the same frozen backbones and AdamW, fp32 trainable weights, no checkpointing): max batch 213 on an L40 at 56.42 samples/s, 409 on an H100 at 192.57

artifacts.scripts: tools/gr00t-batch-search.sh and tools/gr00t-fit.py: the scratchpad's gr00t-smoke.sh and gr00t_fit.py as they ran, with their paths and setup's clone changed
artifacts.results: the scratchpad's gr00t-runs/results.txt and per-run .log and .mem files (not kept)

protocol: docs/86-video-to-robot.md §5.5, after the Isaac-GR00T README's single-GPU method: a fresh process per batch, 7 steps, the median of steps 3 to 7 (forward, backward and AdamW step, synchronized; data loading excluded), the batch doubled from a start until it fails, then bisected to an adjacent pass and failure. A failure is a spill: under WSL the Windows driver moves an overfull card into system RAM instead of raising out-of-memory, so a run whose nvidia-smi memory (sampled every 0.5 s, the desktop included) reached 23,964 MiB, 600 below the card's size, was stopped and counted as failed.
caveats: Fit and speed only: 7 steps say nothing about what a fine-tune learns. Whether 8-bit AdamW state and a bf16 backbone change the result of a real fine-tune is unmeasured; it needs a paired evaluation of policies trained both ways (phase 4).

The ceiling is a spill cutoff, not an out-of-memory error, and it counts the whole card: the desktop's 1.1 to 1.3 GB, and about 0.6 GB more with the Studio open. frozen-lean's 74 and frozen's 4 were found with the Studio open; a run on a native Linux machine with no desktop would fit more.
One workload: NVIDIA's two-camera SO-100 demo. Another embodiment's images, state and action horizon change the per-sample memory.
Step times vary between runs: full-lean batch 32 took 1,644.5 ms in the first search and 1,470.5 ms in the second.
Each run first spends about four minutes decoding the demo's video before step one; that time is outside the step timer, and it is most of a short run's wall clock.

The first full-lean search stopped at batch 64 (a spill recorded as a crash by the script's marker check), and the frozen-lean and frozen runs right after it started while that run still held the card; those are void and not listed. The script now waits for the card to empty and marks spills in their own file; the second search re-ran full-lean from 32.
